item.title: Maloney Westgaard finishes 35th
item.description: Thomas Maloney Westgaard finished in a very respectable 35th in the Cross-Country Skiathlon today at the Winter Olympics. He finished just over three minutes behind the medal positions at the games in Milan/Cortina. Meanwhile, US skiing legend Lindsey Vonn was airlifted off the mountain, after crashing early into her downhill run. Advertisement The 41-year-old was competing despite rupturing her ACL just over a week ago.

item.title: National Hurling League review
item.description: Limerick are off the mark in Division 1A of the National Hurling League. They kept Kilkenny at arms length to run out 1-26 to 2-16 winners at the TUS Gaelic Grounds. Waterford have their second victory of the campaign. Advertisement They were too much for Offaly, coming away from Walsh Park with a 1-19 to 16 point win. === Clare have joined Wexford on top of Division 1B with their third win out of three. item.title: Rangers ease into quarter-finals of Scottish Cup
item.description: Rangers have eased into the quarter-finals of the Scottish Cup by hammering Queens Park 8-nil. The Premiership side were 5-nil up at half-time against their Championship opponents at Ibrox, with captain James Tavernier getting a hat-trick. Stenhousemuir host Falkirk in this evening's fifth round tie. Advertisement

item.title: Kerry County Council invites applicants for Festivals and Participative Events Programme 2026
item.description: Kerry County Council is inviting applications for festival and events grants. The funding supports events that will drive domestic tourism and help to improve the visitor experience in Kerry. €75,000 has been announced by Fáilte Ireland and the council under the Festivals and Participative Events Programme 2026. Advertisement Festivals, voluntary and community groups, chambers of commerce and tourism alliances in the county are urged to apply. The deadline for applications is 5PM on February 16t

item.title: Bohs and Pat’s draw
item.description: Bohemians and St Pats couldn't be separated in today's Men's Premier Division clash at the Aviva Stadium. Neither side found the net in the 0-0 draw. Pats keeper Joey Anang made some crucial stops to give his side a point in their opening game of the year. Advertisement 21 thousand people made the trip to south Dublin for today's game.

item.title: Palace win at Brighton
item.description: Crystal Palace have climbed nine points clear of the Premier League's bottom three with a 1-nil win at rivals Brighton. It ends a run of 12 games without a victory in all competitions. Advertisement
